evidence_tree.command: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <fresh scratch dir>
evidence_tree.isolation: Only data/ and docs/math-foundations.md were read. src/, tests/, scripts/, docs/plans/, docs/receipts/, the diff, and git history were never opened. The scenario definition for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' is NOT present in the evidence tree, so the reconstruction below is structural (ratio-identification) rather than a from-scratch replay of the fight.

step_0_what_can_move_raw_damage_in_this_.claim: Of the two items the scenario is named for, only Bloodsong can change a PRE-MITIGATION raw damage number. Black Cleaver's only damage-side effect is armor reduction, which lives strictly on the mitigation side.
step_0_what_can_move_raw_damage_in_this_.black_cleaver_quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
step_0_what_can_move_raw_damage_in_this_.why_it_cannot_move_raw: docs/math-foundations.md line 242 states the mitigation identity `post = raw · m(R)  ⇺  raw = post · (1 + R/100)`, i.e. resistance (and therefore any armor reduction/penetration) acts only on the raw→post map. A 6%/stack armor shred changes `m(R)`, never `raw`. So the 94.1→101.7 move on a *raw* leaf cannot be a Black Cleaver effect.

step_1_the_only_raw_side_lever_bloodsong.wiki_quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

corroborating_parse.reading: 10 s spellblade window, 100% base AD on-hit, 4 s Expose Weakness duration, 8% / 5% increased damage, 1.5 s cooldown.

rd_template_semantics.convention: {{rd|A|B}} = A for a MELEE holder, B for a RANGED holder.
rd_template_semantics.how_established_from_cache_only: Cross-checked against other {{rd}} uses in data/items.json whose melee/ranged split is well known: Death's Dance {{rd|30%|10%}}, Blade of the Ruined King {{rd|9%|6%}}, Eclipse {{rd|6%|4%}}, Titanic Hydra {{rd|4%|2%}}, Riftmaker omnivamp {{rd|10%|6%}}, Phage move speed {{rd|20|10}}. In every case the first argument is the melee value.
rd_template_semantics.therefore: Expose Weakness = 8% increased damage from all sources for a melee Bloodsong holder, 5% for a ranged one.

step_1_the_only_raw_side_lever_bloodsong.why_it_belongs_on_the_raw_leaf: Expose Weakness is a scalar 'takes X% increased damage' multiplier. docs/math-foundations.md gives mitigation as the scalar map `m(R)=100/(100+R)` and notes it is 'linear in raw damage' for a fixed resistance (Section 1.2 item 1, and the EXACT row for `apply_resistance` in the audit table). A scalar amplifier therefore COMMUTES with mitigation: (1.08·raw)·m(R) == 1.08·(raw·m(R)). Folding Expose Weakness into `raw_damage` is a bookkeeping convention that yields exactly the game's post-mitigation amplified number, so its appearance on a raw leaf is not itself an error.

step_2_ratio_identification.method: The golden stores values rounded to 0.1, so the underlying pre-amp packet B is only known to an interval. Solve for every multiplier k consistent with BOTH roundings: round(B,1)=94.1 (B ∈ [94.05, 94.15)) and round(k·B,1)=101.7 (k·B ∈ [101.65, 101.75)).

candidates_tested.1.05 (Bloodsong Expose Weakness, RANGED: INFEASIBLE — would require B ≈ 96.8, contradicting old = 94.1

step_2_ratio_identification.conclusion: 1.08 is the ONLY round, wiki-sourced multiplier inside the rounding-consistent window. The new value is exactly the old event amplified by Bloodsong's melee Expose Weakness; the old value carried no Expose Weakness amplification at all.
step_2_ratio_identification.rounding_note: Naively 94.1·1.08 = 101.628 → 101.6, and 101.7/1.08 = 94.1667 → 94.2. Neither naive round-trip reproduces the pair, which is expected: both goldens are roundings of the same unrounded B ≈ 94.12–94.15. The interval solve above is the correct check and it closes cleanly.

step_3_scenario_fit.name: cleaver_bloodsong_roster
step_3_scenario_fit.reading: A coupled multi-participant ('roster') timeline holding Black Cleaver + Bloodsong. Expose Weakness reads 'increased damage from ALL sources', i.e. it is a debuff on the target that amplifies every roster participant's damage on it for 4 s — exactly the cross-participant coupling a 'roster' golden exists to pin. An event deep in the timeline (index 39) landing inside a refreshed 4 s Expose Weakness window is the expected state, not the exception.
step_3_scenario_fit.sanity: Black Cleaver (40 AD / 400 HP / 20 AH, physical-damage-gated Carve stacks) plus a support-quest Bloodsong is a melee AD build; the melee branch of {{rd|8%|5%}} is the branch that fits the holder implied by the item pair.

residual_uncertainty: The scenario definition for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' is not in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md, so the pre-amp packet B could not be rebuilt from champion base stats. The identification is therefore by exact-multiplier reconstruction, which is nonetheless decisive: only k=1.08 survives the two roundings, and 8% is a directly wiki-sourced constant of an item this scenario is named for.

The 8%-vs-5% branch depends on the Bloodsong holder being MELEE. That could not be confirmed from the evidence tree alone (no roster champion list). If the Bloodsong holder in this scenario is a RANGED champion, the correct amplifier would be 5% (≈ 98.8) and the verdict would flip to both_wrong. The item pairing (Black Cleaver + a support-quest Bloodsong on the ledger the leaf belongs to) makes the melee branch the strongly indicated reading. Recommended follow-up for whoever owns the change: assert that the engine selects the {{rd}} branch from the holder's attack range rather than hardcoding 8%.
Whether Expose Weakness is folded into `raw_damage` or applied after mitigation is a presentation choice only — it is a scalar and commutes with `m(R)`, so the final damage is identical either way.
bottom_line: 94.1 is the un-amplified packet; Bloodsong's Expose Weakness ('take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources', 4 s) multiplies it by 1.08 for a melee holder, and 1.08 is the unique wiki-sourced multiplier consistent with both rounded goldens. The old value was missing the amplification.
